summary: We may not leave an animal at a non-Jew's inn, and a Jew may not be alone with non-Jews who were suspected of doing bad things. The mishnah also says when a Jewish woman may help a non-Jewish woman with a baby.

chunks.he: אֵין מַעֲמִידִין בְּהֵמָה בְּפֻנְדְּקָאוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם,
chunks.en: We may not leave an animal in the inns of non-Jews,
chunks.st: One may not keep an animal in the inns [befundekaot] of gentiles

chunks.en: because they are suspected of treating animals in a forbidden way.
chunks.st: because they are suspected of bestiality.
chunks.stMore: Since even gentiles are prohibited from engaging in bestiality, a Jew who places his animal there is guilty of violating the prohibition: “You shall not put a stumbling block before the blind” (Leviticus 19:14).

chunks.en: And a woman may not be alone with them,
chunks.st: And a woman may not seclude herself with gentiles

chunks.en: because they are suspected of forbidden relationships.
chunks.st: because they are suspected of engaging in forbidden sexual relations.

chunks.en: And a person may not be alone with them,
chunks.st: And any person may not seclude himself with gentiles

chunks.en: because they are suspected of killing.
chunks.st: because they are suspected of bloodshed.

chunks.he: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְיַלֵּד אֶת הַנָּכְרִית,
chunks.en: A Jewish woman may not help a non-Jewish woman give birth,
chunks.st: A Jewish woman may not deliver the child of a gentile woman,

chunks.en: because she is helping bring a child for avodah zarah.
chunks.explain: The baby will grow up to serve idols.
chunks.st: because in doing so she is delivering a child who will engage in idol worship.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: But a non-Jewish woman may help a Jewish woman give birth.
chunks.st: But one may allow a gentile woman to deliver the child of a Jewish woman.

chunks.he: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תָנִיק בְּנָהּ שֶׁל נָכְרִית,
chunks.en: A Jewish woman may not nurse the baby of a non-Jewish woman,
chunks.st: Similarly, a Jewish woman may not nurse the child of a gentile woman,

chunks.he: אֲבָל נָכְרִית מְנִיקָה בְנָהּ שֶׁל יִשְׂרְאֵלִית בִּרְשׁוּתָהּ:
chunks.en: but a non-Jewish woman may nurse a Jewish woman's baby in the Jewish woman's home.
chunks.st: but one may allow a gentile woman to nurse the child of a Jewish woman while the gentile woman is on the Jewish woman’s property.

summary: We may get healing from a non-Jew for our animals, but not for ourselves. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about getting a haircut from a non-Jew.
stIntro: The mishna discusses the issue of accepting certain professional services from a gentile.

chunks.en: We may get healing from them for our belongings,
chunks.st: One may be treated by gentiles, provided that it is monetary treatment,

chunks.en: but not healing for our own bodies.
chunks.st: but not personal treatment.

chunks.en: And we may not get a haircut from them anywhere,
chunks.explain: We worry he might hurt him with the razor.
chunks.st: And one may not have his hair cut by them anywhere,
chunks.stMore: due to the danger that the gentile will kill him with the razor;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: in a public place it is allowed,
chunks.st: In the public thoroughfare, it is permitted to have one’s hair cut by a gentile,

chunks.en: but not when they are alone together.
chunks.st: but not when the Jew and gentile are alone together.

summary: Some things of non-Jews are so forbidden that we may not even get any use from them, like their wine. Meat going out of an idol's house is forbidden too, and we may not do business with people on their way to an idol's holiday.
stIntro: This mishna discusses the halakhic status of various items that belong to gentiles.

chunks.en: These things of non-Jews
chunks.st: These are items that belong to gentiles

chunks.en: are forbidden, and we may not even get any use from them:
chunks.st: and are prohibited to Jews, and their prohibition is that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited:

words.note: We may not even get any use or money from it.

chunks.he: הַיַּיִן, וְהַחֹמֶץ שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שֶׁהָיָה מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ יַיִן,
chunks.en: their wine, and non-Jews' vinegar that started out as wine,
chunks.explain: It may have been poured out for an idol.
chunks.st: Wine, and vinegar belonging to gentiles that was originally wine,

chunks.en: and Hadrianic clay pots,
chunks.st: and Hadrianic earthenware,

words.note: Clay pieces that had wine soaked into them.

chunks.en: and animal skins with a hole cut by the heart.
chunks.explain: They cut out the heart to offer to their idol.
chunks.st: and hides with a tear opposite the heart.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: when its cut is round, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: A hide is prohibited only when the tear around its heart is circular,

chunks.en: If it is long, it is allowed.
chunks.st: but if it is elongated it is permitted,
chunks.stMore: as gentiles will sacrifice a heart only when it has been removed by a circular laceration.

chunks.en: Meat going into a house of avodah zarah
chunks.st: Meat that enters the house of idol worship

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: is allowed.
chunks.st: is permitted,

chunks.en: But meat coming out is forbidden,
chunks.st: and meat that exits this house is prohibited,

chunks.en: because it is like an offering to dead things — idols.
chunks.st: because it is considered as offerings to the dead, i.e., to idols;

words.note: Idols have no life, so they are called dead.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Those going to an idol's holiday,
chunks.st: With regard to those going to a festival of idolatry [tarput],

chunks.en: it is forbidden to do business with them.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to engage in business with them.

chunks.en: And those coming back are allowed.
chunks.st: And with regard to those who are coming from it, it is permitted to engage in business with them.

summary: Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about some things of non-Jews: are they forbidden even to use, or only to eat?

chunks.en: Wineskins of non-Jews and their jugs,
chunks.st: Wineskins and jugs belonging to gentiles,

chunks.en: with a Jew's wine stored in them,
chunks.st: which have a Jew’s wine contained in them,

chunks.en: are forbidden, and we may not even get any use from them.
chunks.st: are prohibited to Jews, and their prohibition is that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited;

words.note: We may not even get any use or money from it.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they are not forbidden for use.
chunks.st: Their prohibition is not that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited.

chunks.en: Grape seeds and grape skins of non-Jews are forbidden,
chunks.explain: They are left over from making wine.
chunks.st: Residual grape seeds and grape skins belonging to gentiles, which are left behind after the grapes are crushed for wine, are prohibited,

chunks.en: and we may not even get any use from them.
chunks.st: and their prohibition is that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited;

words.note: We may not even get any use or money from it.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: wet ones are forbidden,
chunks.st: Moist grape residues are prohibited,

chunks.en: dry ones are allowed.
chunks.st: but dry residues are permitted.

chunks.he: הַמֻּרְיָס וּגְבִינוֹת בֵּית אֻנְיָקִי שֶׁל גּוֹיִם אֲסוּרִין,
chunks.en: Fish sauce and cheeses from Beis Unyaki that belong to non-Jews are forbidden,
chunks.st: Fish stew [murayes] and cheese of Beit Unyaki belonging to gentiles are prohibited,

words.note: A place.

chunks.en: and we may not even get any use from them.
chunks.st: and their prohibition is that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited.

words.note: We may not even get any use or money from it.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they are not forbidden for use.
chunks.st: Their prohibition is not that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael asked Rabbi Yehoshua why the cheese of non-Jews is forbidden. Rabbi Yehoshua gave reasons, and then turned the talk to a question about a pasuk in Shir HaShirim.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.he: שָׁאַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael asked Rabbi Yehoshua
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael asked Rabbi Yehoshua a series of questions

chunks.en: while they were walking on the road.
chunks.st: while they were traveling along the road.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael said to him:

chunks.en: Why did they forbid the cheeses of non-Jews?
chunks.st: For what reason did the Sages prohibit the cheeses of gentiles?

chunks.en: He answered him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּקֵבָה שֶׁל נְבֵלָה.
chunks.en: Because they make it thick with the stomach of a neveilah.
chunks.st: Because gentiles curdle cheese with the stomach contents of an unslaughtered animal carcass,
chunks.stMore: and as the carcass of an unslaughtered animal is not kosher, cheese that is curdled with it is likewise prohibited.

words.note: An animal that died without shechitah.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: In response, Rabbi Yishmael said to him:

chunks.he: וַהֲלֹא קֵבַת עוֹלָה חֲמוּרָה מִקֵּבַת נְבֵלָה,
chunks.en: But isn't the stomach of a korban olah stricter than the stomach of a neveilah?
chunks.st: But aren’t the stomach contents of a burnt-offering subject to a more stringent prohibition than the stomach contents of an unslaughtered animal carcass?

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: And they said that a Kohen who doesn't mind
chunks.st: And yet they said: A priest who is open-minded [shedato yafa] with regard to what he eats

chunks.en: may swallow it raw.
chunks.st: may swallow [shorefah] the stomach contents of a burnt-offering while they are raw,

chunks.en: But they didn't agree with him.
chunks.st: and the other Sages did not agree with him.

chunks.en: But they did say,
chunks.st: But the Sages said:

chunks.en: we may not get use from it, but one who does has not misused something holy.
chunks.st: One may not derive benefit from the stomach contents of a burnt-offering ab initio, and if one did derive benefit from them, he is not liable for misusing consecrated property.
chunks.stMore: According to both opinions, deriving benefit from the stomach contents of a burnt-offering is not prohibited by Torah law. Since the halakha with regard to a burnt-offering is more stringent than that of an animal carcass, why would deriving benefit from the carcass be prohibited, while deriving benefit from the burnt-offering is permitted?

chunks.en: He turned and said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Yishmael:

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּקֵבַת עֶגְלֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
chunks.en: Because they make it thick with the stomach of calves of avodah zarah.
chunks.st: The cheese of gentiles is prohibited because they curdle it in the stomach contents of calves used for idol worship.
chunks.stMore: Since it is prohibited to derive benefit from such calves, cheese curdled in their stomach contents is also prohibited.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael said to him:

chunks.en: If so,
chunks.st: If that is so,

chunks.en: why didn't they forbid getting any use from it?
chunks.st: why didn’t the Sages prohibit deriving any benefit from the cheese, instead of merely prohibiting its consumption?

chunks.en: He turned him to a different topic,
chunks.explain: He did not want to say the real reason yet.
chunks.st: Instead of answering Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Yehoshua diverted his attention to another matter
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains why he changed the subject.

chunks.en: he said to him,
chunks.st: and said to him:

chunks.en: Yishmael, my brother,
chunks.st: Yishmael,

chunks.en: how do you read this pasuk in Shir HaShirim:
chunks.st: how do you read the following verse in the Song of Songs (1:2)?

words.note: Shir HaShirim, Song of Songs.

chunks.en: "For Your love is better than wine",
chunks.st: Do you read it as: For Your love [dodekha] is better than wine,

chunks.en: or "For your love is better"?
chunks.explain: One way speaks to Hashem, the other to the Jewish people.
chunks.st: or as: For your love [dodayikh] is better than wine?
chunks.stMore: The first version, which is in the masculine form, would be a reference to God, whereas the second version, in the feminine, would be a reference to the Jewish people.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael said to him that it should be read in the feminine:

chunks.en: "For your love is better."
chunks.st: For your love [dodayikh] is better than wine.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

chunks.en: It is not so,
chunks.st: The matter is not so,

chunks.en: because the next words teach about it:
chunks.st: as another verse teaches with regard to it:

chunks.en: "Your oils have a good smell."
chunks.st: “Your ointments [shemanekha] have a goodly fragrance” (Song of Songs 1:3).
chunks.stMore: This phrase, which appears in the next verse, is written in the masculine form, and therefore it is determined that the preceding verse can also be understood in the masculine form.

summary: Some foods of non-Jews are forbidden to eat, but we may still use them or sell them. The mishnah lists them.
stIntro: This mishna lists items belonging to gentiles which it is prohibited to consume, but from which it is permitted to derive benefit.

chunks.en: These things of non-Jews are forbidden,
chunks.st: And these are items that belong to gentiles and are prohibited,

chunks.en: but we may still get use from them:
chunks.st: but their prohibition is not that of an item from which deriving benefit is prohibited:

chunks.he: חָלָב שֶׁחֲלָבוֹ גוֹי וְאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל רוֹאֵהוּ,
chunks.en: Milk that a non-Jew milked when no Jew was watching him,
chunks.st: Milk that was milked by a gentile and a Jew did not see him performing this action,

chunks.en: and their bread and their oil.
chunks.st: and their bread and oil.

chunks.en: Rebbi and his beis din allowed the oil.
chunks.st: The mishna notes that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and his court permitted the oil of gentiles entirely.

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who wrote down the Mishnah.

chunks.he: וּשְׁלָקוֹת, וּכְבָשִׁין שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לָתֵת לְתוֹכָן יַיִן וָחֹמֶץ,
chunks.en: And cooked vegetables, and pickles that people usually put wine and vinegar into,
chunks.st: And boiled and pickled vegetables, whose usual manner of preparation involves adding wine and vinegar to them,

chunks.en: and chopped tarit fish,
chunks.st: and minced tarit fish,

words.note: A kind of fish.

chunks.he: וְצִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ דָּגָה כִלְבִּית שׁוֹטֶטֶת בּוֹ,
chunks.en: and fish sauce that has no kilbis fish floating in it,
chunks.st: and brine that does not have a kilbit fish floating in it,

words.note: A small fish that grows only in kosher fish sauce.

chunks.en: and chilak fish, and a piece of chiltis,
chunks.st: and ḥilak, and a sliver of ḥiltit,

words.note: A kind of small fish.
A kind of plant.

chunks.en: and salkondis salt,
chunks.st: and salkondit salt (see 39b);

words.note: A special salt that had non-kosher fat on it.

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין וְאֵין אִסּוּרָן אִסּוּר הֲנָאָה:
chunks.en: all these are forbidden, but we may still get use from them.
chunks.st: all these are prohibited, but their prohibition is not that of item from which deriving benefit is prohibited.

summary: These foods of non-Jews are allowed to eat, like milk that a Jew watched being milked, and honey.

chunks.en: These are allowed to eat:
chunks.st: And these are permitted for consumption:

chunks.en: Milk that a non-Jew milked while a Jew watched him,
chunks.st: Milk that was milked by a gentile and a Jew watched him doing so;

chunks.en: and honey,
chunks.st: and honey;

chunks.en: and bunches of grapes, even though they drip juice,
chunks.st: and grape clusters [davdevaniyyot] which, despite the fact that they are dripping juice,

chunks.en: the juice does not make them ready to become tamei,
chunks.explain: Food can become tamei only after it gets wet.
chunks.st: are not subject to the halakhot of susceptibility to ritual impurity caused by contact with that liquid;

chunks.he: וּכְבָשִׁין שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן לָתֵת לְתוֹכָן יַיִן וָחֹמֶץ.
chunks.en: and pickles that people do not usually put wine and vinegar into,
chunks.st: and pickled vegetables whose usual manner of preparation does not involve adding wine and vinegar to them;

chunks.en: and tarit fish that is not chopped,
chunks.st: and tarit fish that is not minced;

chunks.en: and fish sauce that has a fish in it,
chunks.st: and brine that has fish in it;

chunks.en: and a leaf of chiltis,
chunks.st: and the leaf of a ḥiltit plant;

chunks.en: and rolled olive cakes.
chunks.st: and rolled olive cakes [geluskaot].

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: very soft olives are forbidden.
chunks.st: Overripe olives are prohibited.

chunks.en: Locusts that come from the seller's basket are forbidden.
chunks.explain: He may have sprinkled wine on them.
chunks.st: Locusts that come from a salesman’s basket are prohibited,

words.note: Some kinds are kosher to eat.

chunks.en: Those from the storeroom are allowed.
chunks.st: whereas those that come from the storeroom [heftek] are permitted;

chunks.en: And the same is true for terumah.
chunks.st: and likewise with regard to the portion of the produce designated for the priest [teruma],
chunks.stMore: as will be explained in the Gemara.
